diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Diabetic nephropathy with hypertensive kidney injury (CKD Stage 4)
supporting_evidence_verified: Disorder of kidney due to diabetes mellitus
Proteinuria & micro-albuminuria attributed to type-2 DM
evidence_gaps: Recent urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio trend
Renal imaging or biopsy if atypical presentation
Historical A1c values >7% to confirm chronic hyperglycemia

supporting_evidence_verified: Essential hypertension since 2007 on three agents (resistant)
evidence_gaps: Renal artery duplex ultrasound or CTA/MRA
Plasma renin activity or aldosterone levels
Detailed home or ambulatory blood pressure readings
concerns: No imaging performed to confirm renovascular disease

evidence_gaps: Temporal correlation of eGFR decline with NSAID exposure
Urine sediment analysis for eosinophils or WBC casts
concerns: NSAID likely a modifier rather than primary cause of Stage 4 CKD

supporting_evidence_verified: Age 64, male, smoker, diabetes, hypertension, metabolic syndrome
evidence_gaps: Resting ECG, lipid panel
Stress test, coronary calcium score, or coronary CTA

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)
evidence_gaps: Echocardiogram with diastolic parameters
BNP or NT-proBNP levels
Documentation of dyspnea, NYHA class, or volume status
concerns: No cardiac imaging or biomarker data to support HFpEF

evidence_gaps: Serum calcium, phosphate, PTH, 25‑OH vitamin D, alkaline phosphatase
concerns: Probability underestimated given eGFR <30 where CKD-MBD is common

supporting_evidence_verified: CKD-related anemia listed as high-priority problem
evidence_gaps: CBC with indices, ferritin, transferrin saturation
ESA use status
Polysomnography or home sleep apnea test
Clinical symptoms such as snoring or daytime sleepiness

supporting_evidence_verified: Metabolic syndrome, CKD, chronic NSAID use
evidence_gaps: Serum uric acid level
History of gout flares or joint examination findings

supporting_evidence_verified: Social stressors (partner abuse, criminal record, occupational stress) noted
evidence_gaps: PHQ-9 or GAD-7 screening scores
Psychiatry or counseling referral documentation
concerns: No formal mental health assessment recorded

consistency_checks.detail: Adjusted probabilities sum to ~1.01, acceptable rounding error.
All severity ≥3 findings except low A1c are linked to at least one diagnosis.

critical_findings_missed: Low A1c = 2.9% (likely data error or overtreatment, not explained)
top_concerns: Overestimation of NSAID nephropathy as primary diagnosis
Absence of renal-artery imaging to evaluate renovascular hypertension
Missing cardiac clearance (CAD/HFpEF) before transplant listing
Unexplained low A1c value requiring repeat testing
recommended_primary: Diabetic nephropathy with hypertensive kidney injury (CKD Stage 4)
review_summary: The differential captures the dominant renal disease and major comorbidities but needs probability rebalancing, addition of renal‑artery evaluation, stronger emphasis on CKD-MBD, and completion of cardiac and metabolic work‑ups before transplant eligibility can be confirmed.
